workEn: The Secret History of the Mongols
title: 元朝秘史 §§24–42
titleEn: The Secret History of the Mongols — §§24–42: Bodonchar Among the Strangers
source: Mongγol-un niγuča tobčiyan (The Secret History of the Mongols), §§24–42, in the Ming Chinese-character phonetic transcription, as edited with a romanized reading by Shiratori Kurakichi 白鳥庫吉, 音訳蒙文元朝秘史 (Tokyo, 1943), itself based on the Ye Dehui 葉德輝 printed edition of 1905/1908; text taken from the Japanese Wikisource transcription, archived and verified against it character for character. Shiratori died in 1942, so the edition was public domain in Japan before the URAA date and was never restored in the United States. Section numbering (§) is the standard citation system. Romanization convention: Shiratori's, kept exactly as he prints it (γ, ġ, ṅ, ž, č, and the raised dot of γ̇). Translations are made fresh from the Mongolian, with the Ming interlinear Chinese glosses as the primary crib. No modern translation was consulted. langCode is null: there is no text-to-speech for Middle Mongol.
about: Bodončar, not counted as kin, rides off down the Onan River, lives on game and a wolf's leavings, with a hawk he has snared, and falls in with a people who ask him nothing. His brother finds him; together they plan a raid on that leaderless people, and Bodončar's captured woman bears sons. The part ends in a run of genealogy, where a clause repeats until it becomes a form. Read for the converb chain (-žu / -žü, the Ming 着), the reflexive-possessive endings (-baγ̇an, -jüġen, -daγ̇an), the plural -nar / -ner and -d / -s (Ming 每), and the possessive -tu / -tü / -tei. Where I could not construe a form with confidence the note says so; the least certain places are §29's first sentence and §27's list of ducks and geese.
draftNote: The Mongol readings follow Shiratori throughout; the English is a first drafting.

sentences.t: Bodončar uruγ-a ese toγ̇aγdažu ende atala jaγ̇un keġežü

morph.gloss: Bodončar (Bodonchar), a man's name; the figure of §§24–42 [(人名)]
not: negates a past action; here before a converb, as ese ögdegsen in the published §6 (compare ülü, which usually negates a converb or non-past) [不曾]
to count, reckon (as in toγ̇an 'counting', Ming 數, in the published §23; the Ming here reads 敎 'teach') [敎]

sentences.l: Bodončar, kin-as not being-counted, here while-staying, what saying,
sentences.i: Not counted as kin, Bodonchar said to himself, “Why stay on here?”
sentences.n: Read this unit as the head of a converb chain: toγ̇aγdažu 'being counted', keġežü 'saying' are -žu / -žü forms, the Ming's 着 (-ing). The chain is long, so I have cut it into short units. uruγ-a is uruγ 'kin' + the dative-locative -a (Ming 行), 'as kin', as in uruγ-a ülü toγ̇an 'not counting as kin' in the published §23. ese is 'not'; it mostly negates a past verb, but here it stands before a converb, which the published part gives to ülü (ülü bolγan, §11): so 'not yet counted', the sense of ese ögdegsen 'not given' in §6. atala is a- 'be' + -tala 'while', Ming 住(間). toγ̇aγdažu is the doubtful word: toγa- 'count' + passive -γda-, 'being counted', fits kin who do not count him, but the Ming glosses it 被敎 'be taught', which I cannot square: 被 is the passive marker, but 敎 (the Ming's stand-in for a causative or an instrumental) is not accounted for by the form. The published part has toγ̇an 'counting' glossed 數, which supports 'count'; I keep 'being counted' and say so. The quoted question is my reading of jaγ̇un keġežü 'what saying'; the Ming just has 甚麽說着.

sentences.t: γol daγ̇aritu γodoli seġültü oroγ šiṅγula-ji unužu

morph.gloss: black-backed, with a black spine (Ming 黑脊) [黑脊]
accusative (after a vowel): the Ming writes 行 [行]

sentences.l: Spine sore-having, bald tail-having, black-backed blue-grey-horse (acc.) riding,
sentences.i: He mounted a blue-grey horse with a sore on its spine, a bare tail and a black back,
sentences.n: The possessive -tu / -tü is the Ming's 有的 'having': daγ̇ari-tu 'sore-having' (Ming 瘡), seġül-tü 'tail-having'. Five words of description (Ming 脊梁瘡有的 禿 尾有的 黑脊 靑白馬) sit before the horse and share it; the final -ji on šiṅγula-ji is the accusative after a vowel, the object of unužu 'riding'. oroγ is the Ming's 黑脊 'black spine'; I take it as 'black-backed' of the horse.

sentences.t: üküġesü in-ü üküsügei aγ̇asu in-ü asuγai

morph.gloss: his, of him: genitive of the 3rd-person pronoun, oblique stem in- + -ü [他的]
optative: let it be (front-vowel form) [也者]
his, of him: genitive of the 3rd-person pronoun, oblique stem in- + -ü [他的]
optative: let it be (back-vowel form) [也者]

sentences.l: If he dies, his dying let-be; if he lives, his living let-be,
sentences.i: “If he dies, let that be his death; if he lives, let that be his life,”
sentences.n: Two conditionals (-ġesü, -γ̇asu, the Ming's 呵 'if') each answered by an optative in -sügei / -suγai (Ming 也者, 'so be it'). The vowel differs with harmony: front üküsügei, back asuγai. in-ü is the genitive of the 3rd-person pronoun, Ming 他的 'his'. Bodončar speaks of himself in the third person ('his dying'); I take it as resignation, 'whatever comes', but that is my reading, not something the Ming says.

sentences.t: keġežü Onan müren huruγ̇u jorčižu talbiba.

morph.gloss: the Onan, a river (the Onon) [(水名)]
downstream, with the current (analysis uncertain) [順水]
to let go, set loose, release [放]

sentences.l: saying, Onan river downstream going, let-go.
sentences.i: so saying, he set off down the Onan River, letting the horse run.
sentences.n: jorčižu talbiba is a pair worth knowing: jorči- 'go, set out' as a converb + talbi- 'let go, release' (Ming 放了). It recurs (here, and in §32) as 'set off', but whether talbi- is literal ('let the horse go') or a light verb 'set off' is my reading; the form does not say. No object is written with talbiba; 'the horse' is my supply, since he is riding. huruγ̇u is the Ming's 順水 'with the stream'; I cannot analyse it.

sentences.t: Jorčižu Balžun-Aral kürčü tende ebesün nembüle ger kižü

morph.gloss: Baljun-Aral, a place on the river; aral is 'island' (compound uncertain) [水名]
a hut, thatched shelter (the Ming has 庵 'hermitage hut') [庵]

sentences.l: Going, Balžun-Aral reaching, there grass hut dwelling making,
sentences.i: Travelling on, he came to Baljun-Aral and made himself a grass hut there,
sentences.n: Three more converbs in -žu / -čü (jorčižu, kürčü, kižü). Balžun-Aral is a place on the water (Ming 水名); aral I take as 'island' but am not sure. ebesün nembüle ger is three nouns in a row, 'grass, hut, dwelling', Ming 草 庵 房子 — apposition without a particle. tende 'there' is tere 'that' + a locative.

sentences.t: tende aba saγ̇uba.

morph.gloss: to sit, settle, live (Ming 生, which can mean 'live, make a living'; the sense is not certain) [生]

sentences.l: there dwelt, settled.
sentences.i: and there he settled and lived.
sentences.n: The chain ends in two finite verbs, aba (a- 'be' + -ba, Ming 住了) and saγ̇uba (Ming 生了). 生 is 'be born', but it also means 'live, make a living', and saγ̇u- 'sit' elsewhere (saγ̇ulžu, published §19; saγ̇uqu-(j)a, Ming 住坐 'live and sit', §39 below) points the same way: I read the two as one idea, 'dwelt, settled', and the 生 as 'live'. That is a reading, not a certainty.

sentences.t: Tein aqui-dur(i)-jan boroγčin qarčiγai qara-quru barižu iden büküi-ji üžežü

morph.gloss: dative-locative: at, in; the (i) is Shiratori's [時分]
reflexive-possessive: one's own (back-vowel form) [part of 住的 時分]

words.reading: 中合舌剌-中忽舌魯 qara-quru

morph.gloss: a kind of wild fowl (Ming 野雞名, 'name of a wild fowl') [野雞名]
participle: the one that is (front-vowel form) [的]

sentences.l: Thus in-his-dwelling-time, fledgling hawk, grouse catching eating being-(acc.) seeing,
sentences.i: While he lived like this, he saw a young hawk that was catching and eating wildfowl,
sentences.n: aqui-dur(i)-jan is a- 'be' + the participle -qui + dative-locative -dur(i) + reflexive-possessive -jan, 'in his own being', Ming 住的 時分 'while dwelling'; the bracketed (i) is Shiratori's. boroγčin is Ming 雛 'chick, fledgling'. qara-quru is a wild fowl (Ming 野雞名, 'name of a wild fowl'; 野雞 in plain Chinese is the pheasant, but I do not know which bird the Mongol word names, so I say 'wildfowl'). büküi-ji is bü- 'be' + participle -küi + accusative -ji, 'the one that was', so the hawk is the object of üžežü 'seeing'.

sentences.t: γol daγ̇aritu γodoli seġültü oroγ sinγula-jin kilγasun-bar qulaγalažu barižu asaraba.

morph.gloss: black-backed, with a black spine (Ming 黑脊) [黑脊]

words.reading: 乞勒中合孫-巴舌兒 kilγasun-bar

morph.gloss: instrumental: with, by means of (back-vowel form) [敎]
to make a noose, snare (Ming 套 'loop, noose') [套]

sentences.l: Spine sore-having, bald tail-having, black-backed blue-grey-horse's tail-hair-with, snaring catching lifted-up.
sentences.i: With hair from the tail of his blue-grey horse, sore along the spine, bare-tailed and black-backed, he snared the hawk and lifted it up.
sentences.n: The same five descriptors as §24, now ending in the genitive -jin (Ming 的) because the horse is the possessor of the tail-hair. kilγasun-bar has the instrumental -bar, 'with, by means of'; the Ming writes 敎, its usual stand-in. Two more converbs (qulaγalažu 'snaring', barižu 'catching') then the finite asaraba 'lifted'. The hawk is never named in the verbs; it is carried over from the previous unit.

sentences.t: Ideküi ideġen ügei arun

morph.gloss: participle: what is (to be) eaten (front-vowel form) [的]
converb: while, when (back-vowel form; compare ügülerün) [時]

sentences.l: Eating-(thing) food without while-being,
sentences.i: With no food to eat,
sentences.n: ideküi is ide- 'eat' + the participle -küi, 'what is to be eaten'; with ideġen 'food' and ügei 'without' it makes 'no food to eat'. arun is a- 'be' + the converb -run, 'while', Ming 住時: the same -run / -rün as in ügülerün 'while saying' (§31).

sentences.t: čino-jin gün-dür qorγaγsan göreġesün marijažu qarbužu alažu

morph.gloss: cliff, steep bank (Ming 崖; analysis uncertain) [崖]

words.reading: 中豁舌兒中合黑三 qorγaγsan

morph.gloss: past participle: that which has been -ed (back-vowel form) [的]
to watch for, stalk (Ming 窺覷 'peer at') [窺覷]

sentences.l: Wolf's cliff-at the-enclosed game, stalking, shooting, killing,
sentences.i: he stalked the game the wolves had hemmed in at a cliff, shot it, and killed it,
sentences.n: qorγaγsan is qorγa- 'enclose' + the past participle -γsan, 'that which was hemmed in', Ming 圍住的; it qualifies göreġesün 'wild animal'. čino-jin is 'the wolf's' (Ming 狼的), singular; I put it in the plural in English. gün is the Ming's 崖 'cliff', analysis uncertain. Three converbs close the unit: marijažu, qarbužu, alažu.

sentences.t: ideldüġed čino-jin idegsen-i temküldüžü ideġed

morph.gloss: jointly, together (the Ming 兼 'and also' may belong to the whole converb: it also glosses ideġed, which has no -ldü-; elsewhere -ldü- is 共) [兼]
past participle: what has been eaten (front-vowel form) [了的]
to pick up, gather (Ming 拾; it may hold -ldü- 'together', but the stem cannot be separated) [拾]

sentences.l: Eating-together, wolf's eaten-(acc.) gathering, eating,
sentences.i: and ate it, gathering up what the wolves had left and eating that too,
sentences.n: -ldü- is 'together, jointly': ideldüġed 'eating along with', and the same element in težiġeldün (§26, below). The Ming glosses both with 兼 'and also', but it glosses ideġed, which has no -ldü-, the same way, and elsewhere -ldü- is 共 (jabulduba, keġeldüžü): so I cannot be sure that the 兼 marks the -ldü-. idegsen-i is 'what has been eaten' + accusative. temküldüžü is the Ming's 拾 'pick up'; it may contain -ldü- but I cannot separate it. The English 'left' is my interpretation of 'what the wolf had eaten'; the Ming gives no 'leftover'.

sentences.t: öġer-ün qoγ̇olai-daγ̇an qarčiγai-baγ̇an ber težiġeldün tere hon γarba.

morph.gloss: dative-locative + reflexive-possessive: to one's own (back-vowel form) [自的(行)]

words.reading: 中合舌兒赤中孩-巴安 qarčiγai-baγ̇an

morph.gloss: reflexive-possessive: one's own, with a dative sense in the Ming (form uncertain) [自的(行)]
jointly, together (here too the Ming 兼 'both, and also' may belong to the whole converb) [兼]
to go out, come up, pass [上去]

sentences.l: Own throat-to, hawk-his-own also, feeding-together, that year went-up.
sentences.i: So he fed himself and his hawk, and that year went by.
sentences.n: Two reflexive-possessives with the Ming's dative sense: qoγ̇olai-daγ̇an 'to his own throat' (喉嚨 自的行), qarčiγai-baγ̇an 'to his own hawk'. The family is -daγ̇an / -baγ̇an / -beġen / -deġen / -jüġen, 'one's own'; watch for it from here on. ber is 'also, even' (Ming 也). γarba is γar- 'go out, rise' + -ba, Ming 上去了 'went up': the year 'went out', that is, passed.

sentences.t: Qabur boluba.
sentences.l: Spring became.
sentences.i: Spring came.
sentences.n: boluba is bolu- 'become' + the past -ba; it is the same verb as bol- in bolba (§32), which Shiratori writes both with and without the linking u. Ming 做了. A bare season noun as subject (qabur, Ming 春) and no copula: 'spring became'.

sentences.t: Noγod ireküi čaγ-tur qarčiγai-baγ̇an teileġülžü oγ̇orba.

words.reading: 中合舌兒赤中孩-巴安 qarčiγai-baγ̇an

morph.gloss: reflexive-possessive: one's own, with a dative sense in the Ming (form uncertain) [自的(行)]
to be hungry (Ming 餓; analysis uncertain) [餓]
to let fly, send off (Ming 放了; the published §19 has the same spelling glossed 去了 'went off') [放]

sentences.l: Ducks coming time-at, hawk-his-own making-hungry, released.
sentences.i: When the ducks came, he made his hawk hungry and then let it fly.
sentences.n: ireküi čaγ-tur: the participle -küi 'coming' qualifies čaγ 'time', and -tur is the dative-locative (Ming 裏), so 'at the time of ducks coming'. noγod is noγu 'duck' + the plural -d (Ming 每). teileġülžü is the Ming's 餓着 'going hungry', with -ġül-, which I take as a causative, 'making hungry'; the Ming shows no 敎 for it, so that rests on the form alone, and the English asks only that the hawk was kept hungry before the flight. I take oγ̇orba as 'let fly' (Ming 放了, and oγ̇oruγ̇ad 飛放 in §28); the same spelling oγ̇orba is glossed 去了 'went off' in the published §19, so the verb may be a general 'send off, go off'.

sentences.t: Noγod γalaγ̇ud qožiγ̇ulas tutun qunsiγ̇ud künžiġüles tutun quṅsiγ̇ud hünistele talbiba.

morph.gloss: (form not analysed) the Ming reads 枯樹 'withered tree' [枯樹]
(form not analysed) the Ming reads 乾樹 'dry tree' [乾樹]
converb: until, up to (front-vowel counterpart of -tala in atala; uncertain); Ming 得 'manage to' [得]
to let go, set loose, release [放]

sentences.l: Ducks, geese, withered-trees each, stench-ones, dry-trees each, fishy-smell-ones, smelling-until, let-go.
sentences.i: Scenting the ducks and geese, he let the hawk go.
sentences.n: The hardest unit of the part. The Ming reads qožiγ̇ulas as 枯樹每 'withered trees', qunsiγ̇ud as 臭氣 'stench', künžiġüles as 乾樹每 'dry trees', quṅsiγ̇ud as 腥氣 'fishy smell', and 每 marks plurals (-d, -s). I cannot make a sentence of 'trees' and 'stench'; the sense must be about the birds' smell, or about how thick they were, and my idiomatic line gives only the frame I am sure of: hünis- 'smell' (Ming 聞) with -tele (Ming 得), then talbiba 'let go' as in §24 (no object is written; 'the hawk' is my supply). The translation is a gloss, not a reading. tutun is Ming 每 'each'; I cannot analyse it.

sentences.t: Düiren gerü-deče Tüṅgelig γoroqan huruγ̇u böleg irgen neġüžü irebe.

morph.gloss: back, behind (Ming 背後; uncertain) [背後]
ablative: from (front-vowel form); the Ming gives no separate gloss, the Han writes the ending in brackets [part of 背後]
downstream, with the current (analysis uncertain) [順水]

sentences.l: Düiren from-behind, Tüṅgelig stream downstream, a-band people, moving-camp, came.
sentences.i: From behind Mount Düiren, down the Tünggelig stream, a band of people came, moving camp.
sentences.n: gerü-deče is the ablative -deče 'from' (the Ming leaves the ending in brackets) on gerü, Ming 背後 'behind'. huruγ̇u again 'downstream'. böleg irgen is 'a band of people', as in the published nigen böleg irgen (§5), not an apposition. neġüžü irebe is a converb + finite verb: 'came moving camp'. Place names: Düiren (mountain), Tüṅgelig (stream), γoroqan 'small river, stream'.

sentences.t: Bodončar tede irgen-dür qarčiγai-baγ̇an oγ̇oruγ̇ad odču

morph.gloss: Bodončar (Bodonchar), a man's name; the figure of §§24–42 [(人名)]

words.reading: 中合舌兒赤中孩-巴安 qarčiγai-baγ̇an

morph.gloss: reflexive-possessive: one's own, with a dative sense in the Ming (form uncertain) [自的(行)]
to let fly (a hawk), go hawking [飛放]
converb: having -ed (linking vowel + -γ̇ad) [part of 飛放]

sentences.l: Bodončar, those people-to, hawk-his-own flying-having, going,
sentences.i: Bodonchar would go to those people, flying his hawk,
sentences.n: tede is the plural of tere 'that'. irgen-dür has the dative-locative -dür (Ming 行). oγ̇oruγ̇ad is the converb -γ̇ad on the hawking verb, Ming 飛放. odču is od- 'go' + the converb -ču, 'going': the only finite verb of the chain is büleġe two units on, so the whole is a habit, as in the speech at §31 ('every day he comes ... and goes').

sentences.t: üdür esüg čiležü

morph.gloss: mare's milk (Ming 馬嬭子) [馬嬭子]

sentences.l: By-day mare's-milk calling-for,
sentences.i: By day he would call for mare's milk,
sentences.n: esüg is the Ming's 馬嬭子 'mare's milk'. čile- is Ming 喚 'call'; I read 'ask for'. Time words stand bare: üdür 'day', süni 'night', no case ending.

sentences.t: süni ebesün nembüle ger-tür(i)-jen irežü qonoqu büleġe.

morph.gloss: a hut, thatched shelter (the Ming has 庵 'hermitage hut') [庵]
past narrative: was, used to be (front-vowel form) [來]

sentences.l: At-night grass hut dwelling-his-own-to coming, spending-night was.
sentences.i: and at night come back to his own grass hut to sleep.
sentences.n: ger-tür(i)-jen: ger 'dwelling' + dative-locative -tür(i) + reflexive-possessive -jen 'own', Ming 房子 自的(行). The last verb is qonoqu büleġe, a participle + the past narrative 'was': 'he used to lodge'. büleġe (bü- 'be' + -leġe, Ming 有來) is the narrative past of habit and report; you will meet it again and again. Its back-vowel pair is -laγ̇a (odulaγ̇a, §30); the pair is my reading.

sentences.t: Tede irgen Bodončar-un qarčiγai γuγ̇asu ese ögbe.

morph.gloss: to ask for, demand (Ming 索; apparently γuju- of the published §6 and §9, with the j lost; uncertain) [索]
ending of the conditional type -γ̇asu, but the Ming gives 着 'converb', not 呵 'if'; uncertain [着]
not: negates a past verb (compare ülü, which negates a converb or non-past) [不曾]

sentences.l: Those people, Bodončar's hawk, asking-(if), not gave.
sentences.i: Those people did not give up Bodonchar's hawk when it was asked for.
sentences.n: I am not sure of this sentence. γuγ̇asu is Ming 索着 'asking for, demanding': a converb gloss (着), not the 呵 'if' the Ming gives this ending elsewhere in the part (aγ̇asu, suraγ̇asu), and the verb looks like γuju- 'ask for' of the published γujuja (§6) and γujužu (§9) with the j lost. Only tede irgen stands in the nominative, so by the grammar the people are the ones who did not give (ese ögbe); my reading is that Bodončar's hawk was asked for and they did not give it up. The opposite (they asked for it and Bodončar refused) is less direct grammatically but cannot be excluded, and the Ming does not say who asks. Either way the unit sets up the next two, which show those people asking nothing about him.

sentences.t: Tede irgen Bodončar-i ken-ü-ġei ba jaγ̇un-u-γ̇ai be keġen asaγqu ügei.

morph.gloss: ending, perhaps 'belonging to' (as in teġün-ü-ġei, published §18); uncertain [part of 誰的]
ending, perhaps 'belonging to' (as -ġei above, back-vowel form); uncertain [part of 甚的]
particle; the Ming has (他) 'he' in brackets; perhaps 'he / it is' (uncertain) [(他)]
converb: saying (quotation marker) [part of 麽道]

sentences.l: Those people, Bodončar (acc.), “whose-?, and of-what-?” saying, asking none.
sentences.i: Those people did not ask Bodonchar, “Whose is he, and of what?”
sentences.n: ken-ü-ġei and jaγ̇un-u-γ̇ai are the genitives of ken 'who' and jaγ̇un 'what' + an ending -ġei / -γ̇ai I cannot identify (Ming 誰的 甚的 'whose, of what'). ba is 'and' (Ming 并). be is a particle: the Ming gives it (他) 'he' in brackets, here and again after the subject in the next unit, so I read a pronoun-like 'he / it is' and keep the question in the third person; I can say no more. The ending -ġei / -γ̇ai is the one in teġün-ü-ġei in the published §18, where I took it as 'belonging to'. keġen 'saying' marks a quotation. asaγqu ügei is the participle 'the asking' + 'none'.

sentences.t: Bodončar be tede irgen-i jaγ̇un irgen keġen asaγ̇ul- čaqu ügei jabulduba.

morph.gloss: Bodončar (Bodonchar), a man's name; the figure of §§24–42 [(人名)]
particle after the subject; the Ming has (他) 'he' in brackets (not 'also'); uncertain [(他)]
converb: saying (quotation marker) [part of 麽道]
reciprocal: one another (the -ul- here; the -ča- follows the hyphen in the next word; as in abulčaba, published §23) [part of 相問]
second half of the reciprocal -ulča- (see asaγ̇ul-); the Ming leaves it blank [(no Ming gloss)]

sentences.l: Bodončar he, those people (acc.), “what people?” saying, asking-one-another none, went-together.
sentences.i: Bodonchar, for his part, did not ask those people, “What people are you?” Neither side put questions to the other, and they travelled together.
sentences.n: asaγ̇ul- čaqu is asaγ- 'ask' + -ulča- + -qu: the reciprocal -ulča- (as in abulčaba, published §23, Ming 相要了) is split here by Shiratori's hyphen after the -ul-, and -qu is the participle; Ming 相問 'ask one another', with nothing for the second half. The split is mine to read, not the Ming's. jabulduba is jabu- 'go' + -ldu- 'together' + -ba (Ming 共行了). The tense and the non-asking in both directions are the point: neither side inquires, and they simply go on.

sentences.n: aqa-juγ̇an is aqa 'elder brother' + the reflexive-possessive -juγ̇an 'own' (the back-vowel counterpart of -jüġen). qoināča is qoina 'behind' + the short ablative -ča (Ming 自 'from'; compare Barγužin-Γoγ̇ača in §8). daγažu is daγa- 'follow'. Three converbs, -žu.

sentences.i: he said: “Elder brother, elder brother! A body with a head, a garment with a collar — that is good.”
sentences.n: A proverb-like pair: teriġü-tü 'head-having', žaqa-tu 'collar-having' (-tü / -tu, Ming 有的), then sain 'good'. I read it as a general truth with a point: a people with no head is like a coat with no collar. The point lands in §35, where Bodončar says the people have no head or hoof. aqa twice, a vocative (the second capital 'Aqa' opens the quotation).

sentences.i: “The people of just now, those on the Tünggelig stream, great and small, bad and good, have neither head nor hoof; they are all alike.
sentences.n: tuγar-un is tuγar 'just now' (Ming 恰纔) + genitive: 'those of just now'. γoroqan-a has the dative-locative -a (Ming 行). bükün is Ming 有的 'being'; I take it as a participle of bü- 'be'. The list is paired: jeke üčügen 'big small', maγ̇ui sain 'bad good'. teriġü šiġira ügeigün is Ming 頭 蹄 無每, 'head, hoof, without-ones'; -gün is a plural (Ming 每). It answers the proverb of §33: a people with no head. The idiom is uncertain: perhaps 'no head and no foot', that is, no leader and no order. sačaġun is Ming 一般每 'all alike'; it ends in the same -ġun / -gün as ügeigün (Ming 每), which is as much as I can say; bükün, with the same ending, has Ming 有的, not 每.

sentences.l: elder-brothers, younger-brothers, consulting, those people (acc.) let-us-plunder saying-together.
sentences.i: we brothers, elder and younger, shall take counsel together and raid those people,” they said in agreement.
sentences.n: aqa-nar and deġü-ner carry the plural -nar / -ner (Ming 每): 'the elder brothers, the younger brothers', the two harmony forms; the pair means 'all our brothers'. They stand without a case ending before ejetüldüžü, so I take them as its subject, 'we brothers consulting together', not as the ones consulted; compare the five brothers as subject in §39. ejetüldü- may belong with ejeten 'of one counsel' (Ming 商量) in the published §22. ejetüldüžü is Ming 商量着 'consulting together'; I cannot analyse the stem. keġeldüžü is keġe- 'say' + -ldü- 'together' (Ming 共說着). Where the quotation ends is not marked; I have closed it here.

sentences.t: ger-tür(i)-jen kürüġed aqa-nar deġü-ner keleleldüžü morilaba.

morph.gloss: to mount a horse (from morin 'horse') [上馬]

sentences.l: Home-his-own-to having-reached, elder-brothers, younger-brothers, conferring-together, mounted.
sentences.i: Reaching their own home, the elder and younger brothers conferred together, and mounted.
sentences.n: kürüġed is kürü- 'reach' (the stem of the published kürüġesü; kür- in kürčü and kürbe above) + -ġed, the front-vowel converb (Ming 了). keleleldüžü is kelele- 'speak' + -ldü- 'together' (Ming 說話共着), the parallel to keġeldüžü; aqa-nar deġü-ner is its subject, as in the previous unit. morilaba is mori-la-ba, 'mounted' (from morin 'horse').

sentences.t: Mün Bodončar-i alginči qaγ̇ulγaba.

morph.gloss: just, the very, indeed (Ming 是 'is'; elsewhere 只那 'that same') [只]

sentences.l: Just-so Bodončar (acc.) as-scout made-run.
sentences.i: And they sent Bodonchar running ahead as the advance scout.
sentences.n: qaγ̇ulγaba is qaγ̇ul- 'rush' + the causative -γa- + -ba, Ming 敎奔去了 'made to run': 'caused to rush ahead'. alginči is Ming 頭哨 'advance scout'. Mün is Ming 只 'just'.

sentences.t: Bodončar alginči qaγ̇ulžu dunda keġelitei eme-ji barižu

morph.gloss: Bodončar (Bodonchar), a man's name; the figure of §§24–42 [(人名)]

sentences.l: Bodončar, as-scout rushing, half-belly-having woman (acc.), seizing,
sentences.i: Bodonchar, rushing ahead as scout, seized a woman half-way through a pregnancy,
sentences.n: dunda keġeli-tei is Ming 半孕 肚皮有的 'half, belly-having', a woman part-way through. eme-ji is 'woman' + the accusative after a vowel; barižu 'seizing' governs it.

sentences.t: Jaγ̇užin küġün či keġen hasaγba.

morph.gloss: of what clan? (Ming 甚氏; from jaγ̇un 'what'?) [甚氏]
converb: saying (quotation marker) [part of 麽道]
to ask (spelt hasaγ- here; the h- is Shiratori's spelling) [問]

sentences.l: “Jaγ̇užin man you,” saying, asked.
sentences.i: and asked her, “Of what clan are you?”
sentences.n: jaγ̇užin is Ming 甚氏 'of what clan'; it comes from jaγ̇un 'what' but I cannot analyse the ending. hasaγba is hasaγ- 'ask' + -ba, with Shiratori's h- (the same verb as asaγ-, §29).

sentences.t: Tere eme ügülerün: "Žarčiγ̇ud- Adanqan Urjaṅqažin bi". keġebe.
sentences.l: That woman saying: “Žarčiγ̇ud, Adanqan, Urjaṅqažin I,” said.
sentences.i: The woman said, “I am a Jarchiud, an Adanqan, an Uriangqajin.”
sentences.n: Three names in a row, Ming 種名 種名 姓(名), 'tribe, tribe, clan'; Shiratori joins the first two with a hyphen. I read them as nested: a Jarchiud woman of the Adanqan, of the Urjaṅqažin clan. bi here is Ming 我 'I' (必), not the 'is' (備) of §35.

sentences.t: Tede irgen-i aqa-nar deġü-ner tabuγ̇ula daγ̇uližu

morph.gloss: five (the final n is lost before -γ̇ula) [五]
all together, the whole lot (compare dörbeġule) [箇]
to plunder (Ming 擄; analysis uncertain) [擄]

sentences.l: Those people (acc.), elder-brothers, younger-brothers, the-five, plundering,
sentences.i: The five brothers, elder and younger, plundered those people,
sentences.n: tabuγ̇ula is tabun 'five' + -γ̇ula 'all together' (Ming 五箇 'five (of them)'), as in the published tabuγ̇ula 'all five' and dörbeġule 'all four'. daγ̇uližu is Ming 擄着 'plundering', another word for 'plunder' alongside qaγ̇ul-. The brothers are the same as in §37.

sentences.t: aduγ̇un ideġen-e haran tudqar-a aqui saγ̇uqu-(j)a kürbe.

morph.gloss: people, persons (Ming 人口 'heads, people') [人口]
servant, one who is ordered about (Ming 使喚) [使喚]
participle: the living [part of 過活]
participle: the sitting [part of 住坐 行]
dative-locative: to (back-vowel form; the j is bracketed) [行]

sentences.l: Horse-herd food-for, people servants-as, living, sitting-to came.
sentences.i: and came to have herds of horses for food and people as servants, to live and settle.
sentences.n: Three datives in -e / -a (Ming 處 / 行): ideġen-e 'for food', tudqar-a 'as servants'; saγ̇uqu-(j)a with the bracketed j. aqui is a- 'live' + -qui as in §25 (Ming 過活), saγ̇uqu 'sitting' (Ming 住坐). kürbe is kür- 'reach, attain': 'they attained a life of living and settling'.

sentences.t: Tere dunda keġelitei eme Bodončar-dür irežü köġülebi.

words.reading: 孛端察舌兒-途舌兒 Bodončar-dür

morph.gloss: to bear a son (from köġün 'son') [兒生]

sentences.l: That half-belly-having woman, Bodončar-to coming, a-son bore.
sentences.i: That woman, half-way through her pregnancy, came to Bodonchar and bore a son.
sentences.n: irežü köġülebi is a converb + a finite verb. köġüle- is Ming 兒生 'bear a son', köġün 'son' + the verb-forming -le-. -bi is a variant of the past -be (Ming 了). The woman is the one captured in §38.

sentences.t: Žad irgen-ü köġün büleġe keġen Žažiradai nereidbe.

morph.gloss: Žad, a people; the Ming has 世人 'people of the world' [世人]
past narrative: was, used to be (front-vowel form) [來]
converb: saying (quotation marker) [part of 麽道]
to provide with (a name); analysis uncertain [與]

sentences.l: “Žad people's son was” saying, son's-name Žažiradai name-gave.
sentences.i: Saying, “He was a son of the Jad people,” he named the boy Jajiradai.
sentences.n: Žad is Ming 世人 'people of the world', I take it as the name of a people, the Jad (compare Žadaran below). büleġe keġen is 'saying: was', a quotation. nereidbe is nere 'name' + a verbal -id- + -be, Ming 名字與了 'gave the name'; the analysis is uncertain.

sentences.t: Žadaran-u ebüge tere boluba.
sentences.l: Žadaran's ancestor that became.
sentences.i: He became the ancestor of the Jadaran.
sentences.n: Žadaran-u is 'of the Žadaran' (Ming 種名的). tere boluba is 'that one became'. ebüge is Ming 祖 'ancestor'.

sentences.t: Tere Žadaradai-jin köġün Tükügüdei neretü büleġe.

morph.gloss: Žadaradai, the same man as Žažiradai (spelling varies) [人名]
past narrative: was, used to be (front-vowel form) [來]

sentences.l: That Žadaradai's son, Tükügüdei name-having, was.
sentences.i: That Jadaradai's son was named Tükügüdei.
sentences.n: Žadaradai is the same man as Žažiradai of §40 (Shiratori's two spellings, in two lines). neretü is nere 'name' + -tü, Ming 名字有的 'having the name': 'son named T.'. The genealogy is a ladder of genitives and sons: X-jin köġün Y büleġe.

sentences.t: Tükügüdei-jin köġün Buribulčiru büleġe.

words.reading: 不舌里不勒赤舌魯 Buribulčiru

morph.gloss: past narrative: was, used to be (front-vowel form) [來]

sentences.l: Tükügüdei's son Buribulčiru was.
sentences.i: Tükügüdei's son was Buribulchiru.
sentences.n: Same ladder. Tükügüdei-jin takes the genitive -jin after a vowel (Ming 的).

sentences.t: Buribulčiru-jin köġün Qara-Qadaγ̇an büleġe.

words.reading: 不舌里不勒赤魯-因 Buribulčiru-jin
中合舌剌-中合荅安 Qara-Qadaγ̇an

morph.gloss: past narrative: was, used to be (front-vowel form) [來]

sentences.l: Buribulčiru's son Qara-Qadaγ̇an was.
sentences.i: Buribulchiru's son was Qara-Qada'an.
sentences.n: Same ladder.

sentences.t: Qara-Qadaγ̇an-(n)ü köġün Žamuqa büleġe.

words.reading: 中合舌剌-中合荅安-訥 Qara-Qadaγ̇an-(n)ü

morph.gloss: genitive: of (front-vowel form) [part of 兒名 的]
past narrative: was, used to be (front-vowel form) [來]

sentences.l: Qara-Qadaγ̇an's son Žamuqa was.
sentences.i: Qara-Qada'an's son was Jamuqa.
sentences.n: The genitive after n is -(n)ü (Ming 的), with the bracketed n in Shiratori's print.

sentences.t: Žadaran oboγtan tede boluba.

morph.gloss: the Žadaran, a clan [一種姓氏]

sentences.l: Žadaran clan-having those became.
sentences.i: They became the clan called Jadaran.
sentences.n: oboγtan is oboγ 'clan' + the plural possessive -tan: Ming 斡孛黑壇 姓(有的)每 'those having a clan-name'. tede boluba 'those became'. This is the formula for the founding of a clan; watch for it in §42.

sentences.t: Tere eme basa Bodončar-ača nigen köġün töreġülbi.

morph.gloss: ablative: from (back-vowel form) [part of (人名) 處]
causative: bring forth, bear [part of 生了]

sentences.l: That woman again Bodončar-from one son bore.
sentences.i: That woman bore Bodonchar another son.
sentences.n: Bodončar-ača has the ablative -ača, Ming 處 'from'. töreġülbi is töre- 'be born' + the causative -ġül- 'bear' + -bi, Ming 生了.

sentences.t: barižu abuγsan eme büleġe. keġen

morph.gloss: past participle: the one who has taken (back-vowel form) [了的]
past narrative: was, used to be (front-vowel form) [來]
converb: saying (quotation marker) [part of 麽道]

sentences.l: Seizing taken-woman was, saying,
sentences.i: Saying, “She was a woman he had seized and taken,”
sentences.n: abuγsan is ab- 'take' (with a linking u; the published §23 has ab-) + the past participle -γsan, Ming 要了的, so 'the taken one'. keġen here, as in §40, closes a quotation (Ming 麽道): the saying gives the reason for the name given in the next unit, as 'he was a son of the Jad people' did in §40.

sentences.t: tere köġün-i Baγ̇aridai nereidbe.

morph.gloss: to provide with (a name); analysis uncertain [與]

sentences.l: that son (acc.) Baγ̇aridai name-gave.
sentences.i: he named that son Ba'aridai.
sentences.n: köġün-i is the accusative (Ming 行). nereidbe as in §40.

sentences.t: Baγ̇arin-u ebüge tere boluba.
sentences.l: Baγ̇arin's ancestor that became.
sentences.i: He became the ancestor of the Ba'arin.
sentences.n: Same shape as §40's 'ancestor of the Žadaran'. The name Baγ̇aridai and the clan Baγ̇arin share a root; the text does not say how.

sentences.t: Baγ̇aridai-jin köġün Čiduqul-Bökö, Čiduqul-Bökö emes olotu büleġe;

morph.gloss: Čiduqul the strongman; bökö is 'wrestler, champion' (Ming 力士) [兒名 力士]
Čiduqul the strongman; bökö is 'wrestler, champion' (Ming 力士) [兒名 力士]
past narrative: was, used to be (front-vowel form) [來]

sentences.l: Baγ̇aridai's son Čiduqul-Bökö, Čiduqul-Bökö women many-having was;
sentences.i: Ba'aridai's son was Chiduqul-Bökö; Chiduqul-Bökö had many women;
sentences.n: Čiduqul-Bökö is repeated at the line break. bökö is Ming 力士 'strongman, wrestler'. emes is eme 'woman' + plural -s. olotu is olo 'many' + -tu, 'having many', Ming 多. The unit ends on büleġe;, with Shiratori's semicolon.

sentences.t: köġün in-ü menemetü törebe.

morph.gloss: his, of him: genitive of the 3rd-person pronoun, oblique stem in- + -ü [他的]
numerous, abundant (Ming 繁多); form not analysed [繁多]

sentences.l: son his abundant was-born.
sentences.i: and his sons were born in great numbers.
sentences.n: menemetü is Ming 繁多 'numerous'; I cannot analyse it. törebe is töre- 'be born' + -be.

sentences.t: Menen-Baγ̇arin oboγtan tede boluba.

morph.gloss: the Menen-Baγ̇arin, a clan [一種姓氏]

sentences.l: Menen-Baγ̇arin clan-having those became.
sentences.i: They became the clan called Menen-Ba'arin.
sentences.n: The same clan formula as §40.

sentences.t: Belgünütei Belgünüd oboγtan boluba.

morph.gloss: the Belgünüd, a clan [一種(姓名)]

sentences.l: Belgünütei, Belgünüd clan-having became.
sentences.i: Belgünütei became the clan Belgünüd.
sentences.n: §42 is five lines in one pattern: a man's name (Ming 人名), the clan (Ming 一種(姓名)), oboγtan 'clan-having', boluba 'became'. The text does not say 'founder' or 'ancestor' and I do not add it: 'X, Y-clan-having, became'. I keep the Mongol's bare 'X became the clan Y'; the plural -tan hints at X's descendants, but the text does not say so.

sentences.t: Bügünütei Bügünüd oboγtan boluba.

morph.gloss: the Bügünüd, a clan [一種(姓名)]

sentences.l: Bügünütei, Bügünüd clan-having became.
sentences.i: Bügünütei became the clan Bügünüd.
sentences.n: Same pattern as the previous unit.

sentences.t: Buγu-Qatagi Qatagin oboγtan boluba.

morph.gloss: the Qatagin, a clan [一種(姓名)]

sentences.l: Buγu-Qatagi, Qatagin clan-having became.
sentences.i: Buqu-Qatagi became the clan Qatagin.
sentences.n: Same pattern. Buγu-Qatagi is the elder brother of §30.

sentences.t: Buγutu-Salži Salžiγ̇ud oboγtan boluba.

morph.gloss: the Salžiγ̇ud (Saljiud), a clan [一種(姓名)]

sentences.l: Buγutu-Salži, Salžiγ̇ud clan-having became.
sentences.i: Buqutu-Salji became the clan Saljiud.
sentences.n: Same pattern. The clan name takes a plural -d (Salžiγ̇ud, as in Belgünüd).

sentences.t: Bodončar Boržigin oboγtan boluba.

morph.gloss: Bodončar (Bodonchar), a man's name; the figure of §§24–42 [人名]

sentences.l: Bodončar, Boržigin clan-having became.
sentences.i: Bodonchar became the clan Borjigin.
sentences.n: Same pattern. The Ming glosses Boržigin only 一種 'a kind', without the 姓名 of the others.
